title: Tech Note: Protecting Against Bad Parameter Counts
author: David Adams

historical_commentary.text: This note documents how classic 4D (interpreted vs. compiled, with/without range checking) behaves when a method is called with the wrong number of parameters — ranging from a syntax error dialog to a hard crash or silently corrupted data — and proposes a defensive Count parameters check plus a centralized ParameterCountIsOkay validator method. The specific compiler behaviors described (crash dialogs, uninitialized-memory reads on OS X/Windows) are tied to the classic 4D compiler and pre-date modern 4D's more robust type system and error handling, but the core defensive-programming discipline of validating parameter counts before use remains directly relevant advice for any procedural or scripting-language codebase, including current 4D code with optional parameters.
related_updates: 4D's language has since added named/typed parameters and other declarative parameter-checking mechanisms in newer versions, reducing (but not eliminating) the need for manual Count parameters checks
The general principle of validating parameter counts/types defensively before use remains standard practice in 4D development today
